subject: Request to revise service availability baseline and credits - Juno Medical
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena@junomed.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@junomed.com>, procurement@junomed.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: availability baseline & monthly credit adjustments for Juno

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile. Procurement and our compliance/legal teams reviewed the standard SLA template you shared. We have two asks we'd like to see reflected in a customer-facing template before we move to signature: 

1) Availability baseline: we have a high-compliance clinical workload and we'd like the baseline availability tightened to 99.99% (monthly). We understand this is above your standard, so we want to find a fair trade-off.

2) Credits and cap: our compliance team prefers a simpler monthly credit schedule with a firm cap tied to our committed spend (not a per-event carveout). Specifically, they propose: 99.99% = no credits; 99.9%–99.0% = 10% monthly credit; <99.0% = 25% monthly credit, with an overall cap of 75% of monthly fees.

We also need a clear statement on maintenance windows (preferably scheduled maintenance windows are excluded from availability calculations if notified 72+ hours in advance) and a statement on data residency and audit logs.

Attached is our procurement team's template with preferred language (Juno_SLA_Request_20261102.pdf) and some simple uptime calculations (uptime_calcs_Juno.xlsx) showing how sensitive our billing is to different thresholds.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept the 99.99% baseline or propose alternate credit math that would be acceptable? If there's a standard exception process or an addendum you use for high-compliance accounts, please share.

Elena
Elena Mendez
Sr. Procurement Manager, Juno Medical
elena@junomed.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Juno_SLA_Request_20261102.pdf (pdf), uptime_calcs_Juno.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Mendez <elena@junomed.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, k_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability baseline & monthly credit adjustments for Juno

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the calc sheet.

Short answer: we can discuss a structured exception but 99.99% baseline is materially above our standard hosted commitment. We try to avoid permanently raising the baseline because that changes routing, capacity commitments, and our dedicated allocation assumptions. That said, there are a few ways we can approach this: 

- Option A (Preferred operational guardrails): Keep standard 99.95% baseline but adjust the credit banding to be more favorable to you once we see steady-state traffic (e.g., reduce credit % for narrow drops).
- Option B (Paid availability uplift): We can offer a 99.99% availability commitment as a paid add-on tied to a reserved capacity/minimum monthly commit. That would come with defined capacity reservations and a monthly premium.
- Option C (Hybrid ride): Start with 99.95% baseline for the first 6 months, with a performance review at month 5 and a commitment to convert to 99.99% (or a credit reduction) if error/latency/traffic patterns are within agreed tolerances.

On maintenance windows: we already exclude scheduled maintenance with 48hr notice; we can extend that to 72hr notice for enterprise-critical plans. Audit logs and data residency are supported for Private deployments — I'll loop in Monica (legal/compliance) to confirm what evidence you need.

I'm copying Aditya (runtime) and Monica (legal) to weigh in on the technical and contractual feasibility. I've attached our customer-facing SLA template so you can see how we usually phrase credits and caps.

Would you be open to a short call to walk through the uptime calculations and the trade-offs for a committed uplift? If so, what days/times next week work for you?

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0789

---

Aditya: realistically, can our hosted offering meet 99.99% with engineering-run routing and burst capacity, or would that require reserved capacity (Dedicated) and extra SRE commitment? Any ballpark premium?

Monica: what language do we need to accept their capped-credit structure (75% of monthly fees)? Our standard limits credits to a smaller percent. Please flag any legal redlines (especially around maintenance, force majeure, credit calculation cadence).

Karthik: pls weigh in on commercial — is this an expansion we can price as a dedicated uplift or should we push the hybrid ride?

I'd like to keep the thread lean when we respond to procurement; propose a 30-min call with Elena next Tue/Wed.

—Jasmine

We favor Option B (paid availability uplift) if the premium is reasonable. The main driver is clinical SLA risk — if we can get a firm 99.99% guarantee with reserved capacity and a clear cap on credits, we can proceed to procure.

If you can provide a short commercial sketch (monthly uplift %, definition of reserved capacity, minimum commit term, and the credit table mapped to our proposed bands), we can review with finance. Also happy to do the call; Tuesday 11/10 at 11:00am PT works.

Elena

Elena — thanks for confirming the call. Per our internal review: 

- Commercial sketch (high level): 99.99% availability as a paid uplift requires a Dedicated reservation (N GPUs) with a minimum 12-month commit. Typical uplift is ~18–22% of committed monthly fees depending on the size of the reservation. We'll provide a custom quote after we confirm expected peak QPS and model footprint.

- Credits: we can accept a fixed-band credit schedule mapped similarly to your proposed bands, with a hard cap equal to 75% of the monthly committed fees for the Dedicated contract. Wording will include an explicit definition of how downtime is measured (per-month measurement window, excluding scheduled maintenance with >=72hr notice and force majeure).

- Operational guarantees: we'll include a monthly incident review, a quarterly performance review, and a clause for temporary traffic rerouting if capacity saturates (with notice).

- Next steps: I'll send a short addendum draft that converts the hosted SLA template into a Dedicated-addendum with the uplift price as a placeholder. Please bring any finance/ops stakeholders to Tue 11/10 11:00am PT so we can confirm sizing.

DocuSign link to the standard Dedicated addendum (draft placeholder) is here: https://app.docusign.com/templates/JUNO-EXP-089

I'll attach the draft addendum and the revised credit table after the call; Monica will push final legal wording.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
